title: Grateful Dead Live at Red Rocks Amphitheatre on 1982-07-27
lineage: FOB - Senn 421's> Sony TC-D5 (at mouth of the stage)> Nak Dragon Playback> HHB CDR-850 (no DAT gen)> CDR

ai_review.summary: A high‑energy Red Rocks summer‑82 show captured on a solid audience tape, with the legendary China > Rider and a monster Playin’/Terrapin/The Other One sequence.
ai_review.review: The performance is widely praised for its daring jams, especially the smoking China Cat → I Know You Rider, the tight Playin’ in the Band sandwich, and an explosive Other One with Phil’s bass bombs. The audience recording is generally good – bright Garcia front‑mic, full venue ambience and occasional mic quirks – making it a very listenable document of one of Red Rocks’ classic nights.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers give 4‑5 stars and highlight exceptional musical moments; recording issues are noted but do not detract significantly, leading to a strong combined rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Bright Garcia mic placement, occasional level jumps and mic fiddling, but clear overall mix that captures Red Rocks ambience; some reviewers note the tape is a bit muddy in places yet remains listenable.

standout_songs: China Cat > I Know You Rider
Playin' in the Band > Terrapin Station > Playin'
show_quality.setlist_flow: First set rolls smoothly with solid tempos; second set builds a high‑impact sandwich centered on Playin' that carries through Terrapin and The Other One before closing with an emotional Stella Blue.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Mic placed directly in front of Garcia, making his guitar bright and prominent; many note his tone is excellent.
band_member_comments.Phil: Lots of praise for Phil’s bass bombs on The Other One and his new four‑string slap technique adding extra power.
band_member_comments.Bob: Unique scat vocal over the beginning of Playing in the Band noted as a rare highlight; drum break described as thrilling.
band_member_comments.Keys: Brent (organ) highlighted for adding intensity on Terrapin Station; keyboards generally full and upfront thanks to venue acoustics.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill’s drum break before the Rhythm Devils chant is called “thrilling”; overall drumming praised for driving the high‑energy jams.
